Thought: To determine how the column dead time in an HPLC system is affected by an increase in the porosity of the column, we need to understand the relationship between porosity and dead time. In HPLC, the column dead time (or void time) is the time it takes for an unretained solute to pass through the column. The porosity of the column refers to the fraction of the column volume that is available for the mobile phase. If the porosity increases, it means there is more space for the mobile phase to flow through, which would typically result in a faster flow and reduced dead time.
